In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on the Surah "Idha Zulzilat" (When the Earth Is Shaken)

It is Meccan, and it is said: it is Madani.

It has been related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] shaking﴾ will have the reward of half the Qur'an credited to him, and whoever recites: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾ will have the reward of a quarter of the Qur'an credited to him, and whoever recites: ﴿Say: He is Allah, [who is] One﴾ will have the reward of a third of the Qur'an credited to him." Abu 'Isa (al-Tirmidhi) related it in his Jami' and said: "This is a gharib (strange) hadith."

He also related, through the narration of Salama ibn Wardan from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, and I have nothing with which to marry." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: He is Allah, [who is] One﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "A third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes, and the victory﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "A quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve﴾?" He said: "Yes."

He said: "A quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] shaking﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "A quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Marry, marry."

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] shaking﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is moved from its lowest part.

Al-Zilzal is intense shaking. It has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas that it occurs after the first blast (of the Trumpet).

In the tafsir it is mentioned that when Israfil blows the first blast into the Trumpet, every thing on the face of the earth is broken by the intensity of his blast, and it enters into the interior of the earth. Then when he blows the second blast, it brings out all that is in its interior and casts it upon its (surface).
And His saying: ﴿And the earth will bring out its burdens﴾ is what we have mentioned, and that is after the second blast. Mujahid and Qatadah said: its treasures and its dead.

"And man will say, 'What is with it?'" That is: the disbeliever will say, "What is wrong with it?" meaning: "What is wrong with the earth that it has brought forth its burdens?"

The disbeliever said this only because he did not believe in the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 99, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾, meaning: it will report what was done upon it, of good and evil. That is, the earth. Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾, and said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will bear witness against every male and female servant for what they did upon its surface, saying: 'He did such-and-such on such-and-such a day.' That is its news."

The imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Naqur informed us: Abu Tahir (ibn) al-Mukhlis informed us: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub... the hadith. And it is said that the meaning is: "And man will say, 'What is wrong with it?'" That is, "What is wrong with the earth that it reports its news?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 99, verse 5:

His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, meaning: He inspired it (ilayha, "to it") that it should relate (its news).

The poet said:

(Awha laha al-qarar fa-staqarrat ...)

Meaning: "to it" (ilayha).

The meaning is that the earth informed (of its news) by the inspiration of God to it.

Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: Revelation (al-wahy, "inspiration" or "revelation") has two senses. The first: God's revelation to His prophets, peace be upon them. The second: in the sense of inspiration (al-ilham), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾, and like this verse, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, meaning: He caused it to be inspired (alhamaha) that it should relate (its news).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 99, verse 6:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿On that Day people will depart in scattered groups﴾ mean: separated from one another.

It is said: "Shatān (شتان) mā bayna fulān wa-fulān" means: how great is the separation between so-and-so and so-and-so.

And His words: ﴿that they may be shown their deeds﴾ mean: their deeds which they had done.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 99, verses 7–8:

And His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: "This verse is the most decisive (muhkam) verse in the Qur'an."

It is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab asked a group of people: "Which verse in the Book of God is the most decisive (muhkam)?" They said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ He said: "Is the son of Umm ʿAbd (Ibn Masʿud) among you?" They said: "Yes." He meant that this (view) was correct from him.

It is related that Sa'sa'a, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and embraced Islam, and he heard this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ He said: "It is enough for me; I do not care if I hear anything else from the Qur'an."

al-Hasan related it as a mursal report.

It is related that al-Mughira ibn Qays narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of God, to what will people come to an end on the Day of Resurrection?' He said: 'To their deeds: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.'"

Regarding the dharra (atom, mote), there are two opinions. One: it is the small red ant, and this is a well-known view. The other: it is what clings to a person's hand when he places it on the ground. It was also said: it is the mote that is seen floating in the air within a window opening in the sunlight. al-Naqqash related from some of them that the dharra is one part of one thousand, four and (twenty) parts of a barleycorn.

It is also related from some of them that he (God) spread many atoms on one of the two pans of the scale, and the pointer of the scale did not tilt.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: [The believer sees his good deeds and his evil deeds; his good deeds are returned to him, and his evil deeds are overlooked.]

It is also related from some of them that the mention of the atom is by way of illustration and comparison, and the meaning is that he will be confronted with his deed, small and great; so what God loves to forgive, He forgives, and what God loves to call to account for, He calls to account. And God knows best.
